purpose: Single source of truth for lakehouse table maintenance: what counts as a small file, how long snapshots are kept, and how long a file must be unreferenced before it is deleted. Every number here was a decision nobody had written down until 2026-08-30, and the tables showed it — 3,160 data files averaging 5 MB, snapshots never expired, orphan cleanup never run.
order_reason: Compaction first, because it is what creates superseded files. Expiry second, because it releases the snapshots that were holding those files. Orphan cleanup last, because it is the only step that reaches files no snapshot ever referenced — the debris a job leaves when it dies mid-write, which expiry cannot see. Run out of order and the debris survives.

compaction.target_file_bytes_reason: 512 MB: the Iceberg default and the size Netflix targets. Below roughly 128 MB the per-file cost of finding, opening and reading a footer starts to outweigh the rows inside; above about 1 GB a file stops splitting across workers. Root ADR-0066.
compaction.min_input_files_reason: A partition holding one file has nothing to merge with. Iceberg skips it either way; stating it keeps the intent legible.
compaction.partial_progress_reason: A compaction commits its file groups in up to this many commits instead of one, so a group that fails (an R2 connection reset, 2026-10-15) keeps the groups already rewritten; the next run takes the rest.
compaction.trigger_reason: Compaction rewrites every byte it touches, so running it on a healthy table costs real money for no gain. Run when at least 10 files sit under a quarter of the target size. Apache Amoro triggers at 40 fragments; ours is lower because our tables are smaller and our loads are less frequent.

snapshot_expiry.retain_reason: Thirty days of rollback (the daily tier), decided by the owner on 2026-10-14 (root ADR-0237); it was seven. Iceberg keeps every superseded data file alive for as long as a snapshot references it, so the window is paid for in R2 bytes — measured before the change from each table's snapshot summaries. `retain_last` guarantees the table never loses its current state even if every snapshot is older than the window.

month_end_tag.reason: Grandfather-father-son, decided by the owner on 2026-10-14 (root ADR-0237): the snapshot `main` pointed at when each month ended (UTC) is tagged and kept for the 12 months after. The maintenance job creates the tag before it expires anything and drops a month-end tag once the month it names is more than `keep_months` months back. Counted by the month the tag names, not by the snapshot's commit time, which is what Iceberg's `RETAIN` would count. No snapshot id is ever listed by hand; an existing tag is never moved.

year_end_tag.reason: December's month-end snapshot is also tagged as the year end and kept forever: the tag has no `max-ref-age-ms`, so `expire_snapshots` never removes it, and the monthly window never reads its name as a month.

reader_pins.reason: Root ADR-0338: whatever reads a snapshot older than the window pins it with an Iceberg tag of its own, made where the data it depends on is committed, released by its own rule; everything else gets the 30 days. Netflix and Iceberg's own documentation keep long-lived references the same way (tags, `max-ref-age-ms`). Expiry never removes a tagged snapshot. A tag marked `walks_main_back_to_it` also keeps every `main` snapshot from the head back to it, because its reader walks that chain; a table listed under `required_on` expires nothing until it carries the tag. `readers` is every code site that reads a snapshot by id, and what keeps that snapshot (test_snapshot_readers_are_pinned).

served-.made_by: crates/publisher/foundation-publisher-by-pnu/src/by_pnu_serving_pins.rs pin (every by-PNU publish, before its manifest is written)
served-.released_by: release_older, once a newer publish of the lane is live
served-.reader: by_pnu_panel_delta.py: the change set from the snapshot the served manifest reflects (root ADR-0146 §2)

baking-.made_by: by_pnu_serving_pins.rs pin_bake (every export shard, before it reads the snapshot the bake pinned)
baking-.released_by: release_behind_live, at the lane's next publish: the generation is then served (and its snapshot holds a served- tag) or abandoned
baking-.reader: the by-PNU exports finishing a generation at its pinned Gold snapshot (root ADR-0310)

foundation-gold-input-.made_by: gold_incremental.retain_input_snapshots, after each Gold producer commit, on every Silver input
foundation-gold-input-.released_by: moved to the new pin by the Gold table's next successful commit; the snapshot it left then has the 30-day window as its grace
foundation-gold-input-.reader: gold_incremental: the next incremental rebuild reads its inputs at the pins the current Gold was built from (root ADR-0180)

foundation-gold-build.made_by: gold_incremental.Outcome.commit, on the producer commit that records the Silver pins
foundation-gold-build.released_by: moved by the Gold table's next producer commit
foundation-gold-build.reader: gold_rebuild.recorded_pins and head_build_pins walk main from the head back to the newest commit that records the Silver pins; only compactions lie between

foundation-floor-history-witness.made_by: building_register_floor_history.pin_witness, once the FLOOR history check has authenticated the witness snapshot
foundation-floor-history-witness.released_by: by hand, with the FLOOR history witness itself; the check reads it on every FLOOR run
foundation-floor-history-witness.reader: building_register_floor_history.verify_append_descendant walks main from the head back to the witness through append commits only

readers.reason: load_baked_snapshot: the snapshot a generation pinned; pin_bake tags it first
read_pinned_iceberg: the current pins (heads this run) and the previous pins an incremental rebuild compares against
read_appended: the appends from the previous pin to the head; a chain with a gap is not an append span and the run compares the two snapshots instead
snapshot_frame: the reflected snapshot and the current one; a missing one refuses the change set (exit 3)
authenticate_history reads the witness snapshot; the other read is the head

read_recorded_append: a retry authenticates the append it recorded; the FLOOR chain keeps the FLOOR's, and any other expired one is refused ("recorded append snapshot is unavailable", root ADR-0332), never re-appended
the host panel's head, which the plan named in this run
main's head, read in the same run
main's head, read in the same run
parcel_lineage's head, read in the same run
the Silver head and the Gold snapshot this run just wrote
the heads this run pinned a moment before
the served Gold head the plan named in this run
main's head; an operator's --price/--exclusive-snapshot-id names its own and fails if it expired
changes_between has no production caller; a missing step returns None and the caller compares two snapshots
an operator's one-off cutover proof (root ADR-0194) at a snapshot the operator names; an expired one fails the query
an operator command at the snapshots the operator names; an expired one fails Trino and nothing is promoted

scheduled.reason: The scheduled job (`lakehouse_maintenance` in orchestration/jobs.v1.json) runs compaction and expiry on every lakehouse contract table, the least recently maintained first. It starts no table after `deadline_minutes`, which stays under the unit's TimeoutStartSec (160m) and Airflow's 165 so a table in flight can finish; a table it does not reach is first at the next run. Orphan cleanup lists a table's whole location and has not been run against R2 from the server; it stays an operator's step until it has. The Spark size is the batch load's (16g driver under the compose `spark` service's 20g cap); the master carries task retries, `local[8,8]`, as every lakehouse job's does (root ADR-0102): plain local[N] ignores spark.task.maxFailures and one R2 connection reset aborted silver.parcel_boundaries on 2026-10-15.

silver.building_register_floors.reason: The FLOOR job authenticates its history by walking from the head back to a witness snapshot through `append` commits only (building_register_floor_history.py `verify_append_descendant`); a compaction commits a `replace` and the next FLOOR run would refuse. Expiry keeps that chain by the `foundation-floor-history-witness` tag (snapshot_expiry.reader_pins, root ADR-0338).

orphan_cleanup.safety_reason: A file that no snapshot references is either debris from a job that died mid-write or output from a job still running. Three days is the industry safety window and Iceberg itself refuses any interval under 24 hours, because deleting a live writer's output corrupts the commit it is about to make.
orphan_cleanup.note: Listing a table's whole location over object storage is slow — a single table timed out past ten minutes from a laptop on 2026-08-30. Run this where the bandwidth is.
